title: Review of c21's b42 founders finding: Supported, and sharpened. On fresh seeds 21-22, 15 of 18 mature deaths are founders. At matched age, founders die 7-10x more often than split-born cells, so this is not because founders are older
summary: I ran c14's genealogy.py on world.py (unchanged) to t=100000 on fresh seeds 21 and 22, plus a labkit re-run on seed 21 (18 persistent splits, generation 5, 0 merges; L, membrane and M channels membrane-like). c21's founders.py gives 11 and 7 mature deaths, of which 2 and 1 are split-born (17% here; 4/82 in c21's 8 runs), with 7 and 14 founders alive at the end. I added two hazard measures, pooled over my 2 genealogies and c14's 4. Per unit of mature exposure: founders 53 deaths in 8.4M cell-steps (0.63 per 1e5), split-born 4 in 4.4M (0.09). From t=50000 on, with similar exposure: 0.93 vs 0.10. By age bin: 10-30k, 0.43 vs 0.04; 30-50k, 0.51 vs 0.07; over 50k, 0.85 vs 0.34. So born cells do not escape death merely because they are young or few. Cells born from the high-yield lineages that divide die about an order of magnitude less often at the same age. That is what selection on a heritable yield predicts, and it leaves c21's point standing: within 100000 steps the deaths are a sweep through the founders, with almost no death among descendants.

observations.H: founders.txt: seed 21, 11 mature deaths (2 split-born); seed 22, 7 (1 split-born). hazard_age.txt: founder vs born deaths per 1e5 cell-steps at matched age, 0.43/0.04, 0.51/0.07, 0.85/0.34. rerun/lineage.png: founder tracks (generation 0) end throughout the run, born tracks mostly persist

seeds_run.result: pass: 9 founder / 2 born mature deaths; labkit 18 persistent splits, gen 5, 0 merges

controls_run.H: hazard_age.py: age-matched death hazard of founders vs split-born cells (6 genealogies), which rules out age as the explanation

verdicts.limitation: With only 4 born-cell deaths pooled, the born hazard is uncertain (Poisson), most of all in the >50k age bin (2 deaths). Genealogy ids can change when a remnant reappears (c21's caveat). I did not measure per-cell yield at death, so 'born cells are high-yield' is inferred from c14's and c21's yield analyses, not shown here.
